title: The Line Studio
award: Site of the Day, Nov 5 2024 + Honors (corpus source: sites_of_the_month; bucket site-of-the-month, award year 2024)
industry: BAFTA-nominated London animation studio (2D/3D animation for commercials, film, games); portfolio + studio site
signature: The UI is built out of animation-desk material: a 24-frame preloader whose loading bar thickens and then settles as the wordmark's crossbar (one stroke that is the H crossbars, both E middle arms and the dash), a red multiply 'acetate' gel laid over the showreel that the first scroll peels away together with the printed wordmark (rotate -15deg about its bottom-left corner) so the same footage appears in full colour, and every panel after that (project sheets, prints, the reel card, the footer) behaving like a paper cel that tilts on a corner pivot and gets flung off, while UI text blinks on in hard frame-steps instead of fading.

first_screen.composition: Full-viewport sticky hero (100svh/100lvh). Showreel video fills 1440x900 and is turned into a red monochrome by a div.acetate above it (background red, mix-blend-mode: multiply). The THE LINE wordmark (inline SVG; block letters with a horizontal bar cutting through all of them, the 'line') spans the full width at the bottom: measured bbox x 18-1420, y 615-878 (~263px tall), fill #e8e9ee (CSS color on .preloader / hero wrapper; pixel-sampled rgb(232,233,238)), sitting ~18px (preloader--home padding 1.27315vw) off the left, right and bottom edges, so it is whole, not cropped. A circled (R) mark floats above its right end (bbox top y 534). Header row on top: small logo left, live studio status 'CLOSED (10-6PM)' with a dot and 'LONDON, ENGLAND' as 10px uppercase labels, inline nav right in 18.33px uppercase separated by '/' with a red dot + red label on the active item. No live text larger than 18px on the first screen: no headline, no CTA. The 10px 'SCROLL TO EXPLORE' label is not a fixed hint; it trails the pointer (element 0 frames). First scroll (verified in the Hero component): the scrub targets the acetate div and the wordmark wrapper, not the video. The acetate is a 100svh non-sticky layer and the video figure sits in .home-hero__sticky (100lvh) inside a 200svh hero whose scroller runs 100svh past it, so the red gel and the logo lift off together on a -15deg tilt and the reel keeps playing, pinned and in full colour, until the 'Highlights' sheet slides over it (desktop_01, mobile_01).
evidence: pixel bbox + colour sample of desktop_00.jpg (audit)

families.name: DenimWeb (Denim variable, self-hosted; @font-face src lists /fonts/DenimVF.woff BEFORE DenimVF.woff2, so browsers download the 103KB WOFF, never the WOFF2; weight axis 300-800)
families.classification: grotesque sans, single family carrying the whole brand
families.source: probe fonts_loaded 'DenimWeb 300 800 normal', font_families_rendered DenimWeb x205, asset_extensions woff:1; inline @font-face in HTML (re-read 2026-09-24)

typography.scale_notes: Measured: section words h1/h3 175px (12.15278vw desktop, 7.2rem = 72px mobile) weight 500; project titles h2 80px weight 470; client run-on list 53px; footer contact 26.67px (.p1 1.85185vw); 'BELLISSIMO' pull quote and news headlines 33px caps (.h5); footer address/social/nav lists 16.67px (.p5 1.15741vw, probe font_sizes 17px x19 = 5+6+8 items); colophon 18.33px (.p4 1.27315vw); nav 18.33px weight 440; body 16px; meta 13px; labels 10px weight 440; bracket counts 8px. Display:label ratio 17.5:1 with almost nothing in between on most screens.
typography.tracking_leading: Display 175px: letter-spacing -7px (-0.04em), line-height 140px (0.8). h2 80px: -3.2px (-0.04em), lh 64px (0.8). Nav 18.33px: -0.18px (-0.01em), lh 0.85. Labels 10px: -0.1px, lh 11.67px. Descenders (the g in 'Highlights') hang into the next row because of lh 0.8.
typography.case_and_style: Sentence case for giant section words ('Highlights', 'The Studio', 'News', 'Credits'); ALL CAPS for nav, labels, status, colophon; every section label is prefixed with a light-weight slash ('/ ABOUT THE LINE', '/ THE LOWDOWN') via .slash-light (slash at weight 300); counts are bracketed superscripts '[ 85 ]' at 8px; arrows are a glyph/SVG after link labels.
signature_moves: One variable family carries everything; SIZE carries the hierarchy (175/80/53/33/27/18/17/13/10/8px) while the weight axis is tuned in odd steps: 500 display, 470 headings and big links, 440 UI and labels, 300 for the slashes
Slash-prefixed section labels and slash-separated nav as a system glyph
Bracketed superscript counts next to links: 'The Work [85] ->'
Giant sentence-case word per section set left at the 7px gutter, lh 0.8
Clients as a 53px run-on sentence separated by ' / ' mixing text names with inline client logo SVGs (Riot Games, Marvel, Mercedes star, Blizzard, Honda)
Preloader counter 'NN/24 fps' set at h1 size, zero-padded

Per-glyph optical margin correction: TextSplitter adds class letter-<first char> to each split display line and a 62-rule table shifts it (e.g. .letter-H/.letter-E/.letter-B -0.07em, .letter-a -0.032em, .letter-j +0.052em) so 175px words sit optically flush on the 6.7px gutter despite side bearings
typography.mobile: h1 72px (probe mobile_measure). Measured from the 2x-DPR mobile_01 screenshot: '/ ABOUT THE LINE' labels ~12px CSS (8px cap height), 'The Work [85]' / 'The Studio' become full-width 24px list rows (.p1 2.4rem; 'The Studio' cap height measured 16.5 CSS px) with the arrow at the right edge and a 1px rule (drawn under 'The Work' in mobile_01); gutter 8px (.8rem). Nav collapses to a 2-bar hamburger; no horizontal overflow. (Earlier values of ~20px labels / 40px rows read device pixels as CSS px.)

color.base: #f8f8f8 (page-bg and meta theme-color); body underneath the sticky layers is rgb(221,222,226) #dddee2
accents: #ff391e brand red-orange: active nav dot+label, hero acetate before preloader completes, footer floor
#ff0000 pure red: acetate multiply layer over video after preloader (transition .3s delay .2s)
#e8e9ee cool near-white: hero/preloader wordmark and '09/24 fps' counter ink, list-open footer sheet
color.ratio: approx 60% #f8f8f8, 15% #0b0b0b ink, 10-15% red floors/tints, rest full-bleed colour of the studio's own animation
color.section_shifts: Red-multiplied reel -> the acetate is peeled off on the first scroll and the same reel plays in full colour -> #f8f8f8 editorial sections -> grey translucent project sheets over full-bleed frames -> full-bleed media -> #f8f8f8 'News' -> #ff391e footer floor that a white logo sheet tilts over. Colour changes arrive as physical sheets sliding over each other, never as gradients.
color.texture: No CSS grain. Texture lives inside the artwork: halftone footer illustration multiplied onto the red floor (mix-blend-mode: multiply, filter grayscale(.3)), print grain inside some animation frames.
color.notes: Awwwards palette #FF391E / #F8F8F8 matches. The multiply acetate is how the site keeps a wildly colourful showreel on-brand: one flat red div, no video grading.

layout.grid: A real 9-column grid on desktop (.grid{grid-template-columns:repeat(9,1fr);gap:0 .46296vw;padding:0 .46296vw}: 6.67px gutters equal to the side margins at 1440) and 5 columns on mobile (.8rem gap and padding). Elements snap to it: header status at col 3 (x 325) and location at col 4 (x 484), awards/about copy and the footer 'Find us' column at col 6 (x 803); about photos col 1/span 3, copy col 6/span 4. The header therefore reads as a 4-slot row (logo | status | location | nav) but is placed on the 9-col grid. css_usage: 4 grid containers, 3 sticky, 3 fixed.
layout.alignment: Hard left to the gutter for all display type; nav hard right.
composition_moves: Giant section word + two arrow links, then a large deliberate void (desktop_01 bottom 200px empty)
Project cards as overlapping tilted paper sheets (desktop_02/03) instead of a grid

Production framing guides drawn over a project card (FieldGuide component): OVERSCAN (dashed) > CROP (solid 1px, with '100%' bottom-right, '[ 16:9 ]' outer label, a centre crosshair and short centre bars) > ACTION SAFE (dashed), each with a live 'W x H' readout ('1573 x ..', '1448 x 969', '1374 x 907' in desktop_02)

Awards and press as two dense 13px uppercase columns at col 6 (left: festivals and awards as underlined links, e.g. ANNECY, CLIO, D&AD; right: press outlets as plain text) beside two studio photos, one flat and one tilted as a print (desktop_04), plus one 33px pull quote 'BELLISSIMO' credited to Guillermo del Toro
Footer as a sticky red floor with the logo on a white sheet that rotates away

Onion-skin sheets: project sheets are rgba(222,223,227,.95), so the full-bleed frame underneath ghosts through at 5% like a light-table/tracing layer (desktop_02: Gorillaz outlines visible through the 'Here, Tomorrow' sheet)

Showreel block (desktop_05 + SSR HTML): the full-bleed muted reel with a centred SQUARE red multiply card (aspect 1/1, 41.84vw = 602px at 1440) carrying film-slate meta in its corners ('SHOWREEL / 2025', '● 1:26', 'THE LINE © MMXXVI', the year converted to Roman numerals by a helper in the bundle) and a '▶ Reel' title with a custom triangle SVG. Press scales the card to .95; open throws the video figure up (translateY -120%, rotate -4deg, 1s cubic-bezier(1,0,.25,.995), .4s delay) and the card to translate(-50%,-200%) rotate(12deg) over 1.2s, leaving a black native player
layout.section_rhythm: Alternates full-bleed moving image (100vh) with a single giant word on white, then a dense list (awards, clients) to reset scale, then full-bleed again.
layout.mobile_adaptation: Single column; sheets keep rotating but with smaller angles (code: rotate -3 vs -7, footer -3deg vs -6deg, translate -24rem vs -16.2vw); nav into hamburger + full-screen menu with a multiply-blended illustration at .5 opacity.

motion.smooth_scroll: Lenis: html.lenis class; bundle nP plugin 'lenis': new Lenis({lerp:.2}), raf driven from gsap.ticker (e.raf(time*1000)), ScrollTrigger.update on every Lenis scroll event.
motion.preloader: Red #ff391e fixed panel (z 500); Lenis is stopped on mount. Timeline (delay .5s): the four fps label parts blink in at 0/.12/.24/.36s via the registered GSAP effect blinkIn (opacity set 0@0, 1@.09, 0@.15, 1@.21: hard frame steps, no tween). A separate counter tween 00 -> 24 over 3s (ease string 'expoInOut', delay .8), toFixed(0).padStart(2,'0'), rendered as '09/24 fps' at h1 size in #e8e9ee. The .logo__line bar (origin left, scaleX 0) grows to scaleX 1 over 1.2s power1.out; at 1.18s it thickens scaleY 3.6 over .35s so it fills the full letter height (frame f01 bar ~74px, f02 ~265px = x3.6); at 1.53s the bar snaps back to scaleY 1, where it IS the wordmark's horizontal crossbar, while the letter groups switch to opacity 1 and their shapes settle from scale 3 / scaleY 3 / scaleX 5 (transform-origin center) to 1 over 1s power4.out, .01s apart per letter; (R) blinks in at 1.8s; the counter blinks out at 2.8s. On home the logo node is appended into .home-hero__wrapper so the loader logo IS the hero logo. On other routes the panel is thrown: yPercent -125, xPercent 10, rotate 15, transformOrigin 'top right', .8s, delay .2, ease pageOut = CustomEase '0.44,0.14,0.28,1'. Total ~3.3s (element video 6.3s including hero reveal).
motion.intro_sequence: Observed frames 0/f00-f07: red panel with only the nav slashes and the cursor label -> '09/24 fps' + thin light bar -> '19/24 fps' + bar thickened into a block -> '23/24 fps' + block resolved into THE LINE wordmark -> a tilted edge (sloping down to the right, ~4deg mid-move) sweeps up the screen, uncovering the red-multiplied showreel UNDER a stationary wordmark -> nav HOME dot and label turn red. Code reading: this is .home-hero__fig (opacity 0, translate(-10%,124%) rotate(15deg)) transitioning to translate(0) rotate(0) over 1s cubic-bezier(.19,1,.22,1) when --visible is added; the acetate swaps #ff391e -> red after .2s.
scroll_techniques: scrub hero peel: the ACETATE layer and the wordmark wrapper (not the video) go to xPercent -10, rotate -15, transformOrigin 'bottom left', ease power1.in, trigger = the acetate, 'top top+=1' to 'bottom top'. The acetate is 100svh and scrolls away; the video figure is sticky, so the gel and logo leave as one printed cel and the reel underneath is left in full colour

scrub intro sheet ('Highlights'): header fromTo {xPercent -10, rotate 8, origin left} -> 0 from 'top bottom' to 'top center'; then the whole block exits to {xPercent -10, rotate -4, yPercent 5, origin right, ease power1.out} from 'top 35%' to 'bottom top-=50%' (enters on one tilt, leaves on the counter-tilt)

scrub featured work entry: wrapper fromTo {yPercent 110, xPercent 15, rotate 15, origin 'top left'} -> 0 and inner asset {yPercent 130, xPercent 20, rotate 15} -> 0 offset .06 (start 'top bottom' end 'top top', ease none, force3D)

scrub featured work exit: wrapper yPercent -80, xPercent -25, rotate -7 (mobile 50/-10/-3); inner asset yPercent -50, xPercent -5, rotate -5 (mobile 40/-2.5/-2), ease none, 'top top+=1' to 'bottom top'

scrub about images: first fromTo {xPercent -45, yPercent 20, rotate 4.89} -> 0, last {xPercent 25, rotate 8} -> {xPercent 45, yPercent -10, rotate 4.89}, ease power1.inOut, start 'top 102%' end 'top 15%'

scrub about header ('The Studio' sheet, .home-about__header-wrapper, not the awards list): fromTo {xPercent -20, yPercent 20, rotate 16, origin left} -> 0, start 'top bottom' end 'top center' (desktop_03 shows it mid-way)

scrub footer wordmark sheet: flat on arrival, peels to {xPercent -7, rotate -6, origin 'top left', ease power1.inOut} from 'top top' to 'max' (mobile {xPercent -14, yPercent -40, rotate -6}) via gsap.matchMedia 1023/1024; footer content parallax yPercent 15 -> 0 over the last screen
stacking: project sheets overlap and slide over full-bleed frames
motion.text_animation: No scroll-scrubbed per-character tweens on the big section words. Small UI text uses stepped opacity 'blink' effects (blink, blinkOnce, blinkIn, blinkOut registered via gsap.registerEffect). SplitText 3.11.3 IS bundled and used through a TextSplitter component (lines / 'lines, words' / chars; lines optionally wrapped in overflow-hidden 'oh' masks, CSS transitionDelay +.1s per line or +.06s per char, split lazily when the block is within 50% of the viewport). Clients list: slash <i> nodes set autoAlpha 1 with stagger .05, then client names .03 (pop-on, no easing). 'Let's Talk' (FooterCta) is split into chars: on mouseenter each char blinks out .025s apart, the label jumps right by the arrow width + 20px and the chars blink back in .025s apart (mouseleave reverses); footer f07 shows this mid-sequence ('Let's  lk').
motion.image_animation: Media never fades or scales in place; it arrives as a rotated sheet translating in from off-canvas (hero fig from 124% down + 15deg) and leaves by rotating on a corner pivot. Reel player open: figure translateY(-120%) rotate(-4deg) with cubic-bezier(1,0,.25,.995); content card to translate(-50%,-200%) rotate(12deg) over 1.2s.
motion.page_transitions: CSS has a fixed .transition-overlay (#0a0a0a66 / hsla(0,0%,4%,.4)) for route changes. Element 2 f05->f07: clicking a Cowboy Bebop card (URL tooltip /work/cowboy-bebop) shifts the grid page aside while a new tilted sheet enters from the bottom (f06; no visible dim in that frame), landing on a case-study hero where a red acetate card is inset over the full-colour key art (f07).
hover_micro: Arrow links (.arrow-link, e.g. 'The Work [85] ->'): the 1px underline is drawn at rest and retracts on hover (scaleX 1 -> 0 with transform-origin swapping left -> right, .8s cubic-bezier(.19,1,.22,1)); the label slides right 2.5463vw; the trailing arrow slides out right (translateX 100%) while a clone arrow slides in at the label's LEFT edge from -100%, both swapped with blinkOut/blinkIn. The arrow relocates from behind the label to in front of it.
Awards links and footer inline links: same underline retract (present at rest, wipes out to the right on hover)
Header location: hovering 'LONDON, ENGLAND' blinks it out and shows 'INFO@THELINESTUDIO.COM' at .33s (and back on leave)
Header logo, status dot, nav colour .6s cubic-bezier(.19,1,.22,1) when the header crosses media vs white
Hamburger: its SVG paths flicker on/off in stepped sets at 0/.08/.16/.35/.43/.51s with .05 stagger, like a hand-drawn boil
Filters: the giant filter word swaps 'All [67]' -> 'Branded. [51]' with a small triangle affordance (element 2 f00/f03); GRID / LIST toggle pills bottom-right (element 2 f05)
motion.cursor: What is visible: a 10px uppercase label that trails the native pointer ('SCROLL TO EXPLORE' on the hero, 'VIEW PROJECT', 'VIEW CASE STUDY', 'VIEW CREW'; element 0/2 frames, desktop_03). CSS also defines .cursor:before{border-radius:50%} (fixed, pointer-events none, shown only under (hover:hover)) but no circle is visible in any screenshot or frame. A cursor-image (hover preview) enters from translateY(10%) rotate(2deg), opacity 0 over .4s cubic-bezier(.19,1,.22,1). CursorCustom follows the pointer on gsap.ticker with a plain lerp of .1 per tick (Rc=.1), starting from the viewport centre, and only under (hover:hover); when a trigger asks for rotation (hasRotation, used by the image previews) it also tilts with horizontal position, rotation mapped from pointer x across the viewport to -10..+10deg (the resize handler remaps to -30..+30deg, an inconsistency in the source). Native cursor not hidden (css cursor_none 0). Custom fixed scrollbar on the right edge (hover:hover): #0b0b0b handle .46296vw wide, min-height 4.63vw, cursor grab.
easing_curves: GSAP defaults ease power2.out; power1.inOut on scrubbed sheets; power4.out for logo settle; expoInOut for counter and bar thickening
motion.stagger_ms: 10 (logo letters), 25 ('Let's Talk' char blink), 30 (client names), 50 (client slashes, hamburger flicker), 60 (TextSplitter chars), 100 (TextSplitter lines), 120 (fps label parts)
motion.choreography_notes: Two motion registers, mostly kept apart: (1) stepped, frame-counted on/off for anything typographic or iconic (blinks at ~2-frame intervals, a nod to animating on twos); (2) heavy, eased or scrubbed physical throws for large surfaces, always with rotation and an off-centre transform-origin (top right, bottom left, top left), entering on one tilt and leaving on the counter-tilt. They meet only in small UI: the arrow link slides AND blinks its arrows, and the cursor image preview fades while it rises and rotates 2deg.

imagery.art_direction: The studio's own frames, full-bleed and uncropped by type: anime-style 2D (Gorillaz, Cowboy Bebop homage, Azuki), stylised 3D (Riot/League), red-toned mecha action in the reel. Tinted to a single red only in the hero via multiply; elsewhere colour is left as delivered. Behind-the-scenes photos (hands, brick wall, keyboard) are shot flat and placed as tilted prints.
treatments: Red acetate: div with background red + mix-blend-mode multiply over video (hero, .home-featured-work__active--acetate, news captions, 404); on the home reel it is a centred square card (desktop_05); on case studies it is an inset card over the full-colour key art, so the frame reads tinted inside the card and in colour around it (element 2 f07)
Production overlays: dashed OVERSCAN / CROP / ACTION SAFE guides with pixel dimensions over a project frame
Small pill chip with a running time beside each work card title (e.g. '00:26'; prefix too low-res in the frames to read reliably)
Halftone illustration multiply-blended on the red footer (filter grayscale(.3))
Photos rotated a few degrees as physical prints

Film-slate metadata on media cards: category / format / '● running time' / date / 'THE LINE © MMXXIV' in 10px caps across the top edge of the acetate card (case study: element 2 f07; home reel card: SSR HTML player-alt__meta, card top is off-screen in desktop_05), years in Roman numerals
imagery.crops_and_ratios: Hero 100svh full-bleed; project sheets roughly 16:9 inside a larger tilted card; work index 2-up (roughly 16:9 and square-ish); news 2-up half-width tiles.

performance_accessibility.weight_notes: Declared: mp4 159.8MB (many videos load lazily / not autoplay), json 1.9MB (Nuxt payload), avif 1.28MB, JS 428KB (main chunk 449KB raw), fonts 103KB: one variable WOFF, because the @font-face lists woff before woff2 (a copy should list woff2 first). Doc height 9613px.
performance_accessibility.reduced_motion: 82 reduced-motion rules: every CSS transition is wrapped in @media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference). Verified in the audit: none of the 27 JS chunks queries prefers-reduced-motion (matchMedia is only used for hover:none, orientation and the 1024px breakpoint), so the preloader, the blink effects and every scroll-scrubbed 7-16deg rotation still run for users who ask for reduced motion.
performance_accessibility.contrast_issues: Brand pair fails WCAG AA for normal text: #f8f8f8 on #ff391e is 3.38:1, used for the 16.67px footer address/social/nav lists, the 18.33px colophon and the 10px column labels; the active nav label #ff391e on #f8f8f8 is also 3.38:1 at 18px. 10px 'SCROLL TO EXPLORE' / 'VIEW PROJECT' in #f8f8f8 over moving video is the weakest small text. The fixed header has no background, so nav and logo overprint content: over the Gorillaz frame (desktop_02), over the awards/press lists (desktop_04) and over the news headlines (desktop_06). #0b0b0b on #f8f8f8 body copy is 18.5:1.
performance_accessibility.mobile_quality: No horizontal overflow at 390px, h1 72px, same sheet physics with reduced angles, video hero kept.

steal_this.technique: Loading bar that becomes the logo
steal_this.why_it_works: The wait is spent assembling the brand mark, so the preloader is not a cover but the first frame of the hero; re-parenting the node means zero visual cut. It only works because the mark was drawn for it: one 90-unit-tall path spans the full 1684-unit viewBox and is at once the H crossbars, both E middle arms and the dash between THE and LINE, so the bar has somewhere to land.
steal_this.how_to_build: Put the preloader over a full-screen accent panel and stop the smooth scroller while it runs. Counter: tween an object {v:0} -> 24 over 3s ease 'expo.inOut' (the bundle writes the name 'expoInOut'), onUpdate write String(Math.round(v)).padStart(2,'0')+'/24 fps' into an h1-sized span. Bar = the wordmark's own crossbar element (height = crossbar height, transform-origin left, scaleX 0). Timeline: scaleX 1 over 1.2s power1.out at t=0; at t=1.18 scaleY = letterHeight/crossbarHeight (3.6 here) over .35s expo.inOut so the bar fills the wordmark box; at t=1.53 set the bar back to scale 1 (it is now the crossbar) and set the letter groups visible, each letter's shapes starting at scale 3 (most shapes: stems, the T bar, the N diagonal), scaleY 3 (the detached E and L horizontal arms) or scaleX 5 (only the L stem), transform-origin center, tweening to 1 over 1s power4.out, .01s per letter. Then appendChild the wordmark wrapper into the hero container so there is no cut, or, off-home, throw the panel: to(panel,{yPercent:-125,xPercent:10,rotate:15,transformOrigin:'top right',duration:.8,delay:.2,ease:CustomEase.create('pageOut','0.44,0.14,0.28,1')}).

steal_this.technique: Frame-stepped blink instead of fades for UI text
steal_this.why_it_works: Reads as animation-on-twos, instantly brand-specific for an animation studio, and costs nothing: no easing, no layout thrash, text is never half-transparent for long.
steal_this.how_to_build: gsap.registerEffect({name:'blinkIn',extendTimeline:true,effect:(t)=>gsap.timeline().set(t,{opacity:0},0).set(t,{opacity:1},.09).set(t,{opacity:0},.15).set(t,{opacity:1},.21)}); blinkOut is the mirror ending at 0. Use tl.blinkIn(el, position) for labels, counters, arrow swaps (blinkOut old arrow + blinkIn new arrow on hover) and a hamburger whose SVG paths flicker with .set calls at 0/.08/.16/.35/.43/.51s, stagger .05. Keep elements visible by default in CSS and only run the blink when JS is ready.

steal_this.technique: Paper-sheet scroll physics on a corner pivot
steal_this.why_it_works: Rotation plus an off-centre transform-origin makes flat DOM panels feel like cels being lifted off a pegbar; one numbers-only rule set gives the whole site its gesture.
steal_this.how_to_build: ScrollTrigger scrub:true, ease 'none' or 'power1.in'. Hero peel: to([acetateLayer,logoWrapper],{xPercent:-10,rotate:-15,transformOrigin:'bottom left',ease:'power1.in'}) from 'top top+=1' to 'bottom top', leaving the video pinned and untouched underneath. Incoming sheet: fromTo(el,{yPercent:110,xPercent:15,rotate:15,transformOrigin:'top left'},{yPercent:0,xPercent:0,rotate:0,ease:'none'}) from 'top bottom' to 'top top', with an inner layer lagging (yPercent 130, xPercent 20, offset .06) so the sheet and its image shear. Outgoing: to(el,{yPercent:-80,xPercent:-25,rotate:-7}) with the inner layer at (-50,-5,-5). Prints: fromTo(img,{xPercent:-45,yPercent:20,rotate:4.89},{xPercent:0,yPercent:0,rotate:0,ease:'power1.inOut'}) start 'top 102%' end 'top 15%'. Use gsap.matchMedia('(max-width:1023px)' / '(min-width:1024px)') for smaller mobile angles (-3/-2). force3D:true; will-change: transform on sheets only while active. Add a prefers-reduced-motion branch the original lacks.

steal_this.technique: Acetate multiply layer to brand-tint any footage
steal_this.why_it_works: One flat div turns an uncontrolled multicolour showreel into a single-hue brand surface without re-grading video, and it can be animated (colour swap) cheaply. Peeling it off on the first scroll then turns the tint into a reveal: the visitor sees the brand colour first and the real work second.
steal_this.how_to_build: .acetate{position:absolute;inset:0;background:#ff0000;mix-blend-mode:multiply;pointer-events:none} placed above the <video> inside the same stacking context (isolation:isolate on the parent). Transition background-color .3s cubic-bezier(.19,1,.22,1) .2s from #ff391e (loader) to #ff0000 (live). Keep light UI text above the acetate, never under it. To reproduce the reveal: make the hero 200svh; put the video in an absolutely positioned scroller that extends 100svh below the hero and holds a position:sticky;top:0;height:100lvh wrapper; make the acetate a separate 100svh absolute layer at the top (not sticky) and put the wordmark in a 100svh flow wrapper; then scrub gsap.to([acetate,wordmark],{xPercent:-10,rotate:-15,transformOrigin:'bottom left',ease:'power1.in'}) from 'top top+=1' to 'bottom top'. The next section slides over the still-pinned colour video.

steal_this.technique: Footer that tilts away to reveal credits
steal_this.why_it_works: The footer becomes a physical object with a back side; a secondary page (credits) is revealed without navigation.
steal_this.how_to_build: Structure: .footer__sticky (position:sticky;top:0;height:100dvh) holds ONLY the red floor and the footer content; the white wordmark sheet is a separate layer above it (z-index 3) and the Credits sheet sits underneath both. Wordmark sheet: ScrollTrigger scrub from 'top top' to 'max': to(sheet,{xPercent:-7,rotate:-6,transformOrigin:'top left',ease:'power1.inOut'}). Credits: on click, lenis.scrollTo(lenis.limit,{duration:.8}), then after .82s add .footer--credits-open: .footer__sticky{transition:transform 1s cubic-bezier(.19,1,.22,1)} .footer--credits-open .footer__sticky{transform:translate(5%,-24rem) rotate(-3deg)} @media(min-width:1024px){...{transform:translate(5%,-16.2037vw) rotate(-6deg)}}; close on the next scroll event or via the big down arrow. Credits sheet: 175px 'Credits' word, roles in the accent colour after accent dot bullets. Wrap the transition in @media (prefers-reduced-motion:no-preference).

steal_this.why_it_works: Dashed overscan/crop/action-safe boxes with pixel sizes are real tools of the trade, so the decoration carries meaning instead of being a generic grid.
steal_this.how_to_build: Three nested absolutely positioned boxes: OVERSCAN (1px dashed currentColor, inset 0), CROP (1px SOLID, ~4% inset) and ACTION SAFE (1px dashed, ~6-7% inset; desktop_02 readouts 1573 -> 1448 -> 1374 wide). Each gets a 10px uppercase label top-left and a 'W x H' readout top-right from Math.ceil(el.getBoundingClientRect()) recomputed on resize; CROP also gets '100%' bottom-right, '[ 16:9 ]' outside its top-left, a centre crosshair and short centre bars. Rotate the whole card with the sheet so guides move with it (note: getBoundingClientRect on a rotated card returns the axis-aligned box, so the numbers are not a true 16:9; that is fine as ornament, wrong as data).

steal_this.technique: Per-letter optical margin table for giant display type
steal_this.why_it_works: At 175px a capital H or E carries ~12px of left side bearing, so a 6.7px gutter looks ragged line to line; shifting each line by its first glyph makes every word sit optically flush on the same edge.
steal_this.how_to_build: Split display headings into lines, read each line's first character and add class `letter-${ch}`; ship a table of `.letter-X{margin-left:-0.0Nem}` values measured per glyph of your face (The Line: H/E/B/D/I/L -0.07em, M -0.068em, a/c/d/e -0.032em, g -0.02em, f -0.006em, j +0.052em). Measure yours by rendering each glyph at 200px against a left rule. Re-apply on resize when lines re-break.

steal_this.why_it_works: The link's trailing arrow jumps to the front of the label as the label slides right, and the underline retracts. It reads as one mechanism instead of a stock arrow nudge.
steal_this.how_to_build: .arrow-link{display:flex;position:relative} label: transition transform .8s cubic-bezier(.19,1,.22,1); :hover label translateX(2.55vw). Main arrow after the label: :hover translateX(100%) + blinkOut. Clone arrow absolutely positioned at left:0, translateX(-100%), opacity 0: :hover translateX(0) + blinkIn. Keep the arrow a custom SVG matched to the type's stroke weight.

steal_this.technique: Cursor label that follows lazily and swings with horizontal position
steal_this.why_it_works: A 10px caps label ('VIEW PROJECT', 'SCROLL TO EXPLORE') trailing the native pointer tells you what a click does without hiding the cursor; the tilt tied to x-position makes the attached image preview hang like a print on a string.
steal_this.how_to_build: Fixed div, pointer-events:none, created only inside gsap.matchMedia('(hover: hover)'). On gsap.ticker: pos.x += (mouse.x - pos.x) * .1; pos.y likewise; if the active trigger wants rotation, rot += (gsap.utils.mapRange(0, innerWidth, -10, 10)(mouse.x) - rot) * .1; gsap.set(el,{x,y,rotation,force3D:true}). Swap the label text on CURSOR:SHOW / HIDE hooks from the hovered element; image previews enter from translateY(10%) rotate(2deg) opacity 0 over .4s cubic-bezier(.19,1,.22,1). Keep one mapRange on resize as well (the original switches to -30..30 after a resize).

slop_risks: Content hidden at opacity 0 until a reveal fires: .header{opacity:0} until .header--visible and .home-hero__fig{opacity:0;transform:translate(-10%,124%) rotate(15deg)} until JS adds --visible after the preloader. If the preloader stalls, nav and hero video never appear. The same trap is wider than the header: every TextSplitter block (.text-splitter{opacity:0} until JS adds --splitted, i.e. the 175px section words, 'Let's Talk', news excerpts and the footer address) and every client name and slash (.home-client i, .home-client__wrapper {opacity:0}) is invisible until JS runs. A copy must default these to visible and only hide under a .js-ready class.

Animated underline: arrow links, awards and footer inline links draw a 1px underline at rest and wipe it out to the right on hover (scaleX 1->0, origin left->right, .8s). It is the retract, not the stock grow-in, and it is paired with the blinking arrow relocation, but the deslop law bans animating underlines at all ('grows, wipes or travels'). A copy should keep the arrow relocation and drop or freeze the underline.

One label treatment, everywhere: 10px uppercase with a slash prefix is used for section kickers, status, location, captions and headings of footer columns. The site gets away with it because nav (18px) and colophon differ, but a naive copy flattens every small string into the same costume.

Text jammed against the edge: the outer gutter is 6.7px at 1440 (.46296vw) and 8px on mobile, so 175px words start almost on the viewport edge. Deliberate Swiss edge here; in a copy without the scale it reads as a missing margin.

Footer wordmark placement: the giant black THE LINE sits ABOVE the link columns (the law wants it flush to the bottom with links above) and is sliced by the viewport bottom mid-scroll (desktop_06). At rest it is whole on both screens (hero 18px clear of the fold, footer end state on the tilted sheet in desktop_07), and the peel-up is what earns the inverted order. Copying the big wordmark-then-content stack without the sheet mechanic is the 'footer wordmark done as slop' tell. The column block itself (four link lists under slash-caps labels plus a colophon row) is the law's 'standard footer'; what redeems it here is the halftone character multiplied across the grid, the red floor and the sheet that tilts away to reveal the credits.
Saturated accent pop: #ff391e plus pure #ff0000 multiply is a full-page system colour here (hero, active nav, floor). Sprinkling one hot red on buttons or icons in a copy is the cheap version.
Rotation as a reflex: every surface tilts; if copied onto content without a physical metaphor (cels, prints, sheets) it becomes gimmicky wobble.

Text you cannot read: the #f8f8f8-on-#ff391e footer (3.38:1) and the #ff391e active nav on #f8f8f8 (3.38:1) fail AA for their 10-18px sizes. A copy must darken the red (or set the footer copy in #0b0b0b, 5.49:1 on #ff391e).
Dot for the active nav item: a red dot before the current link plus a red label. The colour change already carries the state; the dot is the reflex the law calls out. Keep one signal.

Header with no background overprints content (desktop_02/04/06: nav over artwork, over the awards list, logo over news headlines). The site relies on colour swaps; a copy needs a collision rule (hide on scroll-down, or a backing band).

Plain horizontal right arrow as the only link glyph ('The Work [85] ->', 'Newsletter ->', '-> Let's Talk'): acceptable here only because it is a heavy custom SVG with the relocation hover. Lifted as a stock -> it is the arrow tell.
